items.statement: A booking-time model with pre-specified predictors (age, anaesthetic risk class, body mass index, previous nausea with anaesthesia, living alone, travel distance and planned list position) discriminates failed same-day discharge with a c statistic of at least 0.70 on validation data and is well calibrated.
items.rationale: Uses predictors available at booking; the validation threshold reflects the fall seen on validation elsewhere (c4).
items.risks: Too few events if data are limited; list position partly chosen by risk.

items.statement: Moving patients with a high predicted risk to the first half of the list would lower failed same-day discharge.
items.rationale: List position is strongly associated with failure (c3).
items.risks: A prediction model cannot show this causal effect; it needs a later evaluation.

items.statement: Rescue antiemetic doses predict failure as well as nurse-assessed nausea severity.
items.rationale: The proxy is validated for nausea needing treatment (c5).

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 is the prediction target.
